Report exactly what each enforces (conventional commits format, Contentful drift check, secret-guard for .env.sample, blocking direct edits to derived AI config files, etc.) and how they're wired up (husky? core.hooksPath? check package.json "prepare" script or similar).

6. **Test harness config** — vitest.config.*, vitest.setup.ts, playwright.config.*, .storybook/ config, .browserstack.yml — report key settings (coverage thresholds if any, test environment setup, projects configured).
7. **Environment & secrets tooling** — scripts/switchEnv.mjs (what npm run env subcommands exist, the scope:shared|tier|personal|auto tagging, the push-to-GitHub-Environments gate), .env.sample header (full command reference), and how secrets are prevented from leaking (pre-commit secret guard details from step 4).
8. **Contentful sync safety** — scripts/contentful/sync.js and scripts/contentful/content-types/ — confirm the additive-only idempotent behavior claim and any safety checks in the script itself.
9. **Dependency/package protections** — check if there's a Renovate/Dependabot config, and confirm package.json root is Tier 1 per frozenFiles.md.
10. **Docs that encode process guardrails** — read .docs/releaseBranchesRules.md, .docs/architecture.md (just the guardrail-relevant parts: path aliases, overrides pattern boundaries), .docs/upstreamPolicy.md if it exists, and list what's under .docs/memory/ (just filenames + one-line purpose, don't dump contents).
11. **.claude/settings.json** — read it and report any permission rules, hooks, or other harness config configured there.
12. Any other automated guardrail you find that doesn't fit above (e.g. a GitHub branch protection reference in docs, a required-reviewers config, ast-grep or semgrep configs elsewhere).

Report back in a structured format organized by the 12 numbered categories above, with file paths cited for everything. Be thorough but concise — bullet points with concrete facts, not prose. This report will be used to write a comprehensive guardrails document, so completeness and accuracy matter more than brevity, but avoid including full file contents verbatim — extract and summarize the enforcement logic instead.

1	name: Upstream Release Watch
2	
3	# Opens a GitHub issue when @salesforce/retail-react-app ships a new release.
4	# This is an automated notifier — not a drift detector. See .docs/upstream-policy.md
5	# for what to do with the issue (usually: skim release notes, close, update
6	# .docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md).
7	
8	on:
9	  schedule:
10	    - cron: '0 0 * * 1'  # Every Monday at midnight UTC
11	  workflow_dispatch:      # Allow manual trigger for testing
12	
13	permissions:
14	  issues: write
15	  contents: read
16	
17	jobs:
18	  check-upstream-release:
19	    name: Check for new PWA Kit upstream release
20	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
21	
22	    steps:
23	      - name: Checkout
24	        uses: actions/checkout@v4
25	
26	      - name: Fetch latest upstream release tag
27	        id: upstream
28	        run: |
29	          RESPONSE=$(curl -sf \
30	            -H "Accept: application/vnd.github+json" \
31	            -H "X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2022-11-28" \
32	            https://api.github.com/repos/SalesforceCommerceCloud/pwa-kit/releases/latest)
33	          LATEST_TAG=$(echo "$RESPONSE" | jq -r '.tag_name')
34	          RELEASE_URL=$(echo "$RESPONSE" | jq -r '.html_url')
35	          PUBLISHED_AT=$(echo "$RESPONSE" | jq -r '.published_at' | cut -c1-10)
36	          echo "tag=$LATEST_TAG" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
37	          echo "url=$RELEASE_URL" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
38	          echo "published=$PUBLISHED_AT" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
39	
40	      - name: Read baseline tag from upstreamBaseline.md
41	        id: baseline
42	        run: |
43	          BASELINE_TAG=$(grep -oP '(?<=<!-- upstream-release-tag: )[^\s]+(?= -->)' .docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md || echo "UNSET")
44	          echo "tag=$BASELINE_TAG" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
45	
46	      - name: Check for existing open issue for this release
47	        id: existing
48	        env:
49	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
50	        run: |
51	          COUNT=$(gh issue list \
52	            --label "upstream-sync" \
53	            --state open \
54	            --json title \
55	            --jq '.[].title' \
56	            | grep -c "${{ steps.upstream.outputs.tag }}" || true)
57	          echo "count=$COUNT" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
58	
59	      - name: Open tracking issue
60	        if: |
61	          steps.upstream.outputs.tag != steps.baseline.outputs.tag &&
62	          steps.existing.outputs.count == '0'
63	        env:
64	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
65	        run: |
66	          LATEST_TAG="${{ steps.upstream.outputs.tag }}"
67	          RELEASE_URL="${{ steps.upstream.outputs.url }}"
68	          PUBLISHED="${{ steps.upstream.outputs.published }}"
69	          BASELINE_TAG="${{ steps.baseline.outputs.tag }}"
70	
71	          gh issue create \
72	            --title "Upstream release available: $LATEST_TAG" \
73	            --label "upstream-sync,needs-review" \
74	            --body "$(cat <<EOF
75	          ## New Salesforce PWA Kit release detected
76	
77	          | | |
78	          |---|---|
79	          | New upstream release | [$LATEST_TAG]($RELEASE_URL) |
80	          | Published | $PUBLISHED |
81	          | Current baseline | $BASELINE_TAG |
82	
83	          ---
84	
85	          ## What to do
86	
87	          Our policy is **bump opportunistically, not on a schedule.** See [.docs/upstream-policy.md](../blob/main/.docs/upstream-policy.md).
88	
89	          1. Open the [release notes]($RELEASE_URL).
90	          2. Skim for:
91	             - **Security** — CVE fixes, dependency patches we are exposed to.
92	             - **SDK** — changes in \`pwa-kit-runtime\`, \`pwa-kit-react-sdk\`, \`commerce-sdk-react\`, or \`pwa-kit-dev\` that affect code we use.
93	             - **Bug fixes or features** we have been waiting for.
94	          3. **If nothing relevant:** close this issue with a one-line reason, and update \`Reviewed up to\` in [.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md](../blob/main/.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md). Do not bump.
95	          4. **If something relevant:** bump \`@salesforce/retail-react-app\` (and any related SDK packages), run \`npx tsc --noEmit\`, \`npm run build\`, \`npm run test\`, then update **both** \`Current\` and \`Reviewed up to\` (and the \`<!-- upstream-release-tag: ... -->\` marker) in upstreamBaseline.md.
96	
97	          ---
98	
99	          _Opened automatically by the upstream-release-watch workflow._
100	          EOF
101	          )"
102	
103	      - name: Log no-op reason
104	        if: |
105	          steps.upstream.outputs.tag == steps.baseline.outputs.tag ||
106	          steps.existing.outputs.count != '0'
107	        run: |
108	          if [ "${{ steps.upstream.outputs.tag }}" = "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.tag }}" ]; then
109	            echo "No new release. Latest upstream (${{ steps.upstream.outputs.tag }}) matches current baseline."
110	          else
111	            echo "Issue already exists for ${{ steps.upstream.outputs.tag }}. No duplicate created."
112	          fi

1	name: Weekly Agents
2	
3	on:
4	  schedule:
5	    - cron: '0 1 * * 1'   # Every Monday at 1am UTC (after upstream-release-watch at midnight)

7

12	
13	jobs:
14	  quality-sweep:
15	    name: Quality sweep — missing tests or stories
16	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
17	    steps:
18	      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
19	
20	      - name: Find components and hooks without paired tests/stories
21	        id: sweep
22	        run: |
23	          missing=()
24	
25	          # Components under overrides/app/components/ — TypeScript only per AGENTS.md.
26	          # Per Zimmermann convention every UI component must have a paired .stories.tsx;
27	          # a .test.ts(x) is required for logic-heavy components but not for every leaf.
28	          # Flag any component file that lacks BOTH a story and a test.
29	          while IFS= read -r file; do
30	            base="${file%.*}"
31	            dir=$(dirname "$file")
32	            name=$(basename "$base")
33	            found=false
34	            # Check for paired test or story (same basename or co-located in the same folder)
35	            for t in "${base}.test.ts" "${base}.test.tsx" "${base}.stories.tsx" \
36	                     "${dir}/${name}.test.ts" "${dir}/${name}.test.tsx" "${dir}/${name}.stories.tsx" \
37	                     "${dir}/index.test.ts" "${dir}/index.test.tsx" "${dir}/index.stories.tsx"; do
38	              [[ -f "$t" ]] && found=true && break
39	            done
40	            $found || missing+=("$file")
41	          done < <(find overrides/app/components \
42	            \( -name "index.tsx" -o -name "index.ts" \) \
43	            ! -path "*/node_modules/*" 2>/dev/null | sort)
44	
45	          # Hooks: look for use-*.ts (override convention keeps kebab-case) and useFoo.ts
46	          # (Zimmermann camelCase convention) without a paired test file.
47	          while IFS= read -r file; do
48	            base="${file%.*}"
49	            found=false
50	            for t in "${base}.test.ts" "${base}.test.tsx"; do
51	              [[ -f "$t" ]] && found=true && break
52	            done
53	            $found || missing+=("$file")
54	          done < <(find overrides/app/hooks \
55	            \( -name "use-*.ts" -o -name "use[A-Z]*.ts" \) \
56	            ! -path "*/node_modules/*" 2>/dev/null | sort)
57	
58	          # Write results
59	          COUNT=${#missing[@]}
60	          echo "count=$COUNT" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
61	
62	          if [[ $COUNT -gt 0 ]]; then
63	            printf '%s\n' "${missing[@]}" > /tmp/missing-tests.txt
64	            echo "has_missing=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
65	          else
66	            echo "has_missing=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
67	          fi
68	
69	      - name: Check for existing open quality-sweep issue
70	        id: existing
71	        if: steps.sweep.outputs.has_missing == 'true'
72	        env:

1	#!/bin/bash
2	# Pre-commit hook:
3	#   1. Regenerate the Claude Code registry and stage any changes.
4	#   2. If any Studio Experiences component (experiences/*.tsx) is staged,
5	#      regenerate definitions.ts and stage it automatically.
6	#   3. Protect derived configuration files from direct edits.
7	#   4. Block .env.sample commits that contain secret-class key values.
8	#
9	# Setup: hooks are managed by Husky v9 — run `npm install` and they are installed automatically.
10	#   Husky sets core.hooksPath to .husky/_ and .husky/pre-commit calls this script.
11	#   If you ever need to install manually (e.g. npm install --ignore-scripts):
12	#   cp scripts/hooks/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
13	#   cp scripts/hooks/commit-msg .git/hooks/commit-msg && chmod +x .git/hooks/commit-msg
14	
15	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
16	# 0. Ensure node is on PATH.
17	#    Git hooks run in a non-interactive shell — version managers (nvm, fnm,
18	#    volta) are not sourced automatically. Try each in turn; fail loudly if
19	#    node still can't be found so the developer knows what to fix.
20	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
21	
22	if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
23	  # nvm (most common on macOS)
24	  export NVM_DIR="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
25	  [ -s "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh" ] && \. "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh"
26	
27	  # fnm
28	  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null && command -v fnm &>/dev/null; then
29	    eval "$(fnm env 2>/dev/null || true)"
30	  fi
31	
32	  # volta
33	  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
34	    export PATH="$HOME/.volta/bin:$PATH"
35	  fi
36	
37	  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
38	    echo "  ❌  pre-commit: node not found. Make sure your version manager is"
39	    echo "      initialised (nvm, fnm, or volta) and node is installed."
40	    exit 1
41	  fi
42	fi
43	
44	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
45	# 1. Registry regeneration — runs on every commit to keep .claude/registry/
46	#    in sync. Stages any updated registry files automatically.
47	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
48	
49	staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only)
50	
51	registry_components=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/components/' || true)
52	registry_hooks=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/hooks/' || true)
53	registry_utils=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/utils/' || true)
54	registry_pages=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/pages/' || true)
55	registry_routes=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/routes\.(tsx|jsx)$' || true)
56	
57	if [ -n "$registry_components$registry_hooks$registry_utils$registry_pages$registry_routes" ] \
58	  && command -v node &>/dev/null && [ -f "scripts/generateRegistry.mjs" ]; then
59	  echo "Regenerating Claude Code registry..."
60	  node scripts/generateRegistry.mjs
61	  git add .claude/registry/
62	fi
63	
64	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
65	# 1b. AI rules sync — when a .claude/ source file is staged, auto-regenerate
66	#     the derived files (.cursor/rules/, .vscode/instructions/,
67	#     .github/copilot-instructions.md) and stage the updates. Only the "auto"
68	#     targets are regenerated; manual targets remain untouched.
69	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
70	
71	if command -v node &>/dev/null && [ -f "scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs" ]; then
72	  ai_sources_staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only \
73	    | grep -E '^\.claude/(rules/.*\.md|skills/.*/SKILL\.md)$' \
74	    || true)
75	
76	  if [ -n "$ai_sources_staged" ]; then
77	    echo "AI rule source(s) changed — running sync:ai-rules:fix..."
78	    node scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs --fix > /dev/null
79	    git add .cursor/rules/ .vscode/instructions/ .github/copilot-instructions.md 2>/dev/null || true
80	  fi
81	fi
82	
83	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
84	# 1c. Skill inventory sync reminder — when a skill is added, removed, or
85	#     changed, remind the developer to update .claude/skills/README.md (the
86	#     canonical skill reference) and the mirrored Confluence page. Warning
87	#     only — there is no Confluence API integration wired up to verify this
88	#     automatically.
89	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
90	
91	skill_files_staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only \
92	  | grep -E '^\.claude/skills/[^/]+/SKILL\.md$' \
93	  || true)
94	
95	if [ -n "$skill_files_staged" ]; then
96	  echo ""
97	  echo "Skill file(s) changed:"
98	  echo "$skill_files_staged" | sed 's/^/  - /'
99	
100	  if ! git diff --cached --name-only | grep -qF '.claude/skills/README.md'; then
101	    echo ""
102	    echo "  ⚠️  .claude/skills/README.md is not staged — update it to match"
103	    echo "     (see 'Adding a new skill' at the bottom of that file)."
104	  fi
105	
106	  echo ""
107	  echo "  ⚠️  Reminder: also update the mirrored Confluence page (child page under"
108	  echo "     page ID 297140226, \"Claude Code Skills Reference\") — there is no"
109	  echo "     automated push from this repo to Confluence yet."
110	  echo "  Committing anyway — this is a warning only."
111	  echo ""
112	fi
113	
114	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
115	# 2. Contentful Studio Experiences codegen
116	#    When any experiences/*.tsx file is staged, regenerate definitions.ts
117	#    and stage it automatically. Blocks the commit on codegen failure.
118	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
119	
120	experiences_staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only \
121	  | grep -E 'overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/.*\.tsx$' \
122	  || true)
123	
124	if [ -n "$experiences_staged" ]; then
125	  echo "Studio Experiences component staged — regenerating definitions.ts..."
126	
127	  REAL_EXPERIENCES="overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences"
128	  tmp_exp=$(mktemp -d)
129	  trap 'rm -rf "$tmp_exp"' EXIT
130	
131	  # Populate temp dir with the staged version of each .tsx.
132	  # Files that are not staged are copied from the working tree so the generator
133	  # sees a complete set. definitions.ts is excluded — it is the output target.
134	  for f in "$REAL_EXPERIENCES"/*.tsx; do
135	    [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
136	    name=$(basename "$f")
137	    [[ "$name" == "definitions.ts" ]] && continue
138	    if echo "$experiences_staged" | grep -qF "$f"; then
139	      git show ":0:$f" > "$tmp_exp/$name"
140	    else
141	      cp "$f" "$tmp_exp/$name"
142	    fi
143	  done
144	
145	  if ! CF_EXPERIENCES_DIR="$tmp_exp" node scripts/contentful/generateDefinitions.mjs; then
146	    echo ""
147	    echo "  ❌  Contentful codegen failed. Fix the errors above and try again."
148	    exit 1
149	  fi
150	
151	  cp "$tmp_exp/definitions.ts" "$REAL_EXPERIENCES/definitions.ts"
152	  git add "$REAL_EXPERIENCES/definitions.ts"
153	  echo "  ✓  definitions.ts updated and staged."
154	fi
155	
156	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
157	# 3. Derived configuration file guard
158	#    Blocks commits that directly edit derived files (.cursor/rules/,
159	#    .vscode/instructions/, .github/copilot-instructions.md) without also
160	#    staging the .claude/ source they were generated from.
161	#    Only triggers on MODIFIED files (diff-filter=M) — newly created derived
162	#    files are allowed through so the initial sync commit is not blocked.
163	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
164	
165	blocked_files=()
166	
167	# Get all MODIFIED (not newly added) staged files
168	modified_staged=$(git diff --cached --diff-filter=M --name-only || true)
169	
170	while IFS= read -r file; do
171	  [[ -z "$file" ]] && continue
172	
173	  # Only check files in derived locations
174	  case "$file" in
175	    .cursor/rules/*|.vscode/instructions/*|.github/copilot-instructions.md) ;;
176	    *) continue ;;
177	  esac
178	
179	  # Only check if the file exists and contains a synced-from comment
180	  [[ ! -f "$file" ]] && continue
181	  synced_line=$(grep -m1 'synced-from:' "$file" 2>/dev/null || true)
182	  [[ -z "$synced_line" ]] && continue
183	
184	  # Extract all source paths from the synced-from comment
185	  # Format: <!-- synced-from: path/to/source.md[, path2, ...] — ... -->
186	  synced_sources=$(echo "$synced_line" \
187	    | sed 's/.*synced-from:[[:space:]]*//' \
188	    | sed 's/[[:space:]]*—.*//')
189	
190	  [[ -z "$synced_sources" ]] && continue
191	
192	  # If ANY source is also staged in this commit, this is a legitimate sync
193	  # update — the developer edited a .claude/ source and ran the sync script.
194	  # Skip it.
195	  staged_names=$(git diff --cached --name-only)
196	  any_source_staged=false
197	  while IFS= read -r src; do
198	    src=$(echo "$src" | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//;s/[[:space:]]*$//')
199	    [[ -z "$src" ]] && continue
200	    if echo "$staged_names" | grep -qxF -- "$src"; then
201	      any_source_staged=true
202	      break
203	    fi
204	  done <<< "$(echo "$synced_sources" | tr ',' '\n')"
205	  if $any_source_staged; then
206	    continue
207	  fi
208	
209	  # Source is NOT staged — this derived file was edited directly.
210	  blocked_files+=("$file")
211	
212	done <<< "$modified_staged"
213	
214	if [ "${#blocked_files[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
215	  echo ""
216	  echo "  ❌  Commit blocked — derived configuration file(s) edited directly:"
217	  echo ""
218	  for bf in "${blocked_files[@]}"; do
219	    echo "       $bf"
220	  done
221	  echo ""
222	  echo "  These files are generated from .claude/ sources and must not be edited directly."
223	  echo ""
224	  echo "  To update auto-generated rules:"
225	  echo "    1. Edit the .claude/ source (see the synced-from comment at the top of the file)"
226	  echo "    2. Run: node scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs --fix"
227	  echo "    3. Commit the .claude/ source and the regenerated file together"
228	  echo ""
229	  echo "  To propose changes to .claude/ master files or sync rules:"
230	  echo "    Raise the request to the Tech Lead via #dev-team"
231	  echo ""
232	  exit 1
233	fi
234	
235	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
236	# 4. .env.sample secrets guard
237	#    Blocks commits where a secret-class key has a non-empty value, or where
238	#    a value matches a known credential pattern (JWT, long hex, base64, provider
239	#    prefixes). Runs only when .env.sample is staged.
240	#    Secret-class key names: *_SECRET, *_TOKEN, *_PASSWORD, *_CREDENTIAL,
241	#    *_PRIVATE_KEY, *_API_KEY, *_BEARER, *_SIGNING_KEY, *_ENCRYPTION_KEY,
242	#    *_DSN, *_WEBHOOK_SECRET.
243	#    Non-secret public identifiers (ORG_ID, SITE_ID, SHORT_CODE, CLIENT_ID,
244	#    SPACE_ID, ENVIRONMENT_ID, OCAPI_HOST) may keep placeholder values.
245	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
246	
247	if git diff --cached --name-only | grep -qF '.env.sample'; then
248	  secret_violations=()
249	
250	  while IFS= read -r line; do
251	    [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*# ]] && continue
252	    [[ -z "${line// }" ]] && continue
253	    [[ "$line" =~ ^([A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*)=(.*)$ ]] || continue
254	    key="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
255	    value="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
256	    [[ -z "$value" ]] && continue
257	
258	    # Secret-class key name with a non-empty value
259	    if echo "$key" | grep -qE '(_SECRET|_TOKEN|_PASSWORD|_CREDENTIAL|_PRIVATE_KEY|_API_KEY|_BEARER|_SIGNING_KEY|_ENCRYPTION_KEY|_DSN|_WEBHOOK_SECRET)'; then
260	      secret_violations+=("  $key  (secret-class key name with non-empty value)")
261	      continue
262	    fi
263	
264	    # Value looks like a JWT
265	    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$'; then
266	      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a JWT)")
267	      continue
268	    fi
269	
270	    # Value looks like a hex credential (32+ pure hex chars)
271	    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^[0-9a-fA-F]{32,}$'; then
272	      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a hex credential)")
273	      continue
274	    fi
275	
276	    # Value looks like a base64 credential (40+ chars)
277	    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9+/]{40,}={0,2}$'; then
278	      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a base64 credential)")
279	      continue
280	    fi
281	
282	    # Known provider-specific key prefixes
283	    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^(AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}|ghs_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}|sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{32,}|xox[bpars]-[A-Za-z0-9-]+)'; then
284	      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value matches a known provider secret format)")
285	      continue
286	    fi
287	
288	  done < <(git show ":0:.env.sample" 2>/dev/null || true)
289	
290	  if [ "${#secret_violations[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
291	    echo ""
292	    echo "  ❌  Commit blocked — .env.sample contains secret-class key(s) with non-empty values:"
293	    echo ""
294	    for v in "${secret_violations[@]}"; do
295	      echo "    $v"
296	    done
297	    echo ""
298	    echo "  .env.sample must only contain blank values for secret-class keys."
299	    echo "  Non-secret public identifiers (ORG_ID, SITE_ID, etc.) may keep their values."
300	    echo ""
301	    echo "  Remove the value(s) above, re-stage .env.sample, and commit again."
302	    echo ""
303	    exit 1
304	  fi
305	fi
306	
307	exit 0

1	# Git hooks
2	
3	Two hooks ship in this folder:
4	
5	- **`pre-commit`** — regenerates `.claude/registry/`, warns on Contentful definition drift, blocks direct edits to derived AI-config files (`.cursor/rules/`, `.vscode/instructions/`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`) when their `.claude/` source is not also staged, warns when a skill (`.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md`) changes without `.claude/skills/README.md` also staged and reminds to update the mirrored Confluence page (no automated push exists yet), and **blocks** any commit where `.env.sample` has a non-empty value for a variable whose name looks like a secret (`TOKEN`/`SECRET`/`KEY`/`PASSWORD`/`CREDENTIAL`) — real values belong only in `.env` (gitignored).
6	- **`commit-msg`** — enforces conventional commits (`type(scope): description`). Allowed types: `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `style`, `refactor`, `perf`, `test`, `build`, `ci`, `chore`, `upstream-sync`.
7	
8	## Install
9	
10	Husky wires these in automatically on `npm install` via the `prepare` script in `package.json`. The Husky-managed wrappers live in [`.husky/pre-commit`](../../.husky/pre-commit) and [`.husky/commit-msg`](../../.husky/commit-msg) and just delegate to the scripts here.
11	
12	If Husky did not install (e.g. cloned with `--no-install` or hooks are not running), install manually:
13	
14	```bash
15	cp scripts/hooks/pre-commit  .git/hooks/pre-commit  && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
16	cp scripts/hooks/commit-msg  .git/hooks/commit-msg  && chmod +x .git/hooks/commit-msg
17	```
18	
19	## Bypass
20	
21	Hooks should not be bypassed. If a hook fails, fix the underlying issue rather than running `git commit --no-verify` — see [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) hard rule 13.

2	
3	How we handle new releases of `@salesforce/retail-react-app` (and the surrounding PWA Kit SDKs).
4	
5	## Principle
6	
7	**Bump opportunistically — not on a schedule.** Stay on the current version unless a release contains something we actually care about.
8	
9	Reasons to bump:
10	- **Security** — CVE fix, dependency patch with a known vulnerability, advisory we are exposed to.
11	- **SDK** — a change in `pwa-kit-runtime`, `pwa-kit-react-sdk`, `commerce-sdk-react`, or `pwa-kit-dev` that affects code we depend on (SSR, routing, hooks we use, build pipeline).
12	- **Bug fix or feature we have been waiting for** — a fix to behaviour we currently work around, or a feature that lets us delete custom code, or will help us on implementing a planned feature.
13	
14	Reasons **not** to bump:
15	- A release with only template/UI changes that we have already overridden.
16	- A release whose changelog touches packages or paths we do not use.
17	- "It's been a while."
18	
19	## Discipline
20	
21	When the upstream-release-watch workflow opens a tracking issue (see [.github/workflows/upstream-release-watch.yml](../.github/workflows/upstream-release-watch.yml)):
22	
23	1. Open the linked release notes.
24	2. Skim for the three categories above.
25	3. If nothing relevant, close the issue with a one-line reason and update `Reviewed up to` in [.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md](memory/upstreamBaseline.md). **Do not bump.**
26	4. If something relevant, bump — then update `Current` and `Reviewed up to` together.
27	
28	## What we do not do
29	
30	- **No drift detection script.** We do not diff our `overrides/` against the upstream template on a schedule. Drift is the *point* of the overrides pattern.
31	- **No two-track review.** There is no separate "SDK package review" vs "template code skim." If we bump, we bump; the changelog tells us what to test.
32	- **No bump because it's been N weeks.** Time alone is not a reason.
33	
34	## Related
35	
36	- Current baseline: [.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md](memory/upstreamBaseline.md)
37	- Watch workflow: [.github/workflows/upstream-release-watch.yml](../.github/workflows/upstream-release-watch.yml)
38	- CI security gate (once CI lands): `npm audit --audit-level=high` — fail on new highs only.

204	## Integration Map

206	All order-creation, fulfilment write, and CRM sync traffic from SFCC routes through MuleSoft as the middleware layer — SFCC does not call NewStore, AP21, Omneo, or Narvar directly. 208	**Boundary key:**

249	## Cross-Storefront Session & Basket Scope
250	
251	All eight storefronts are path-prefixed on a single first-party domain and share one SFCC realm with shared customer data. The `httpOnly` SLAS refresh-token cookie set by the SSR layer is therefore presented on every storefront prefix — no cross-domain SSO bridge is needed. SLAS tokens are channel-scoped, so the SSR layer re-initialises the SLAS context per storefront; a registered shopper is silently re-recognised across a storefront switch (shared customer record), while a guest session is site-scoped and does not carry over. **The basket deliberately does not transfer across storefronts** — baskets are site-scoped and priced in the storefront's own currency/pricebook, so a shopper switching storefront starts a fresh basket. Carrying a basket across a currency boundary would produce incorrect pricing. The Global-e checkout handoff is a separate session boundary (Global-e owns its hosted checkout in full). The exact SLAS re-authorisation mechanism and the stay-signed-in UX are open items with the Salesforce integration team.
252	
253	## Customer Data Migration (DMU-004, updated 2026-05-29)
254	
255	Only **email + Omneo customer ID** are migrated into SFCC at go-live. All other customer profile data — name, phone, addresses, communication preferences — is sourced **live from Omneo at login** via MuleSoft. Implication: My Account profile pages cannot rely on SFCC for the full customer record; an Omneo round-trip is required post-authentication. Graceful degradation for Omneo outages becomes load-bearing on account screens. Asset/CDN migration (DMU-010) is **de-scoped** — images stay in Contentful, no asset 301s.
256	
257	## Blast-Radius Mitigation
258	
259	Multiple upstream integrations (SFCC, MuleSoft/Omneo, Global-e, Narvar, Contentful, Didomi, Inside Chat) mean a failure or attack targeting one service must not cascade. A PWA-relevant mitigation can be done in the SSR layer.
260	
261	The SSR layer in `overrides/app/ssr.js` uses **Node's native `fetch`**, which is backed by `undici`. Undici's `dispatcher` option (the per-call `dispatcher` option on individual `fetch()` invocations) allows each upstream origin to be given its own connection pool with an independent cap. This prevents a slow or flooded integration (e.g. checkout APIs) from exhausting connections for unrelated origins (e.g. Contentful, JWKS).
262	
263	```ts
264	import { Pool } from 'undici';
265	
266	// 1. Create isolated pools for specific origins
267	const checkoutPool = new Pool('https://api.checkout-service.com', {
268	  connections: 10, // Hard limit of 10 concurrent connections to this origin
269	  timeout: 8000,
270	});
271	
272	// 2. Use them explicitly in your fetch calls inside ssr.js
273	async function getCheckoutMetadata() {
274	  return await fetch('https://api.checkout-service.com/v1/metadata', {
275	    dispatcher: checkoutPool, // Safely isolated!
276	  });
277	}
278	```

1	# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://coderabbit.ai/integrations/schema.v2.json
2	# .coderabbit.yaml — Zimmermann PWA Kit
3	# CodeRabbit configuration for AI-assisted PR review
4	# Docs: https://docs.coderabbit.ai/configuration
5	#
6	# Paths target this slim overrides project: `overrides/app/...` (not the upstream monorepo
7	# `packages/template-retail-react-app/app/...`). Hooks under `overrides/` are `.ts` per the
8	# TypeScript-only rule.
9	#
10	# NOTE: `version: "2"` and a top-level `custom_instructions:` block previously lived here.
11	# Neither key exists in the current schema (schema.v2.json) — confirmed by validating
12	# against the published schema and cross-checking real production configs (appsmith,
13	# bruno, MONAI), none of which use either key. custom_instructions's 12 rules have been
14	# migrated to the path_instructions entry below so they actually take effect.
15	
16	# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
17	# LANGUAGE & TONE
18	# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
19	language: "en-US"
20	
21	reviews:
22	  # Post a high-level summary on every PR
23	  high_level_summary: true
24	
25	  # Post a poem... no. We're engineers.
26	  poem: false
27	
28	  # Collapse walkthrough for smaller PRs to reduce noise
29	  collapse_walkthrough: false
30	
31	  # Request changes (not just comment) when critical issues found
32	  request_changes_workflow: true
33	
34	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
35	  # PROFILE — sets the overall review strictness
36	  # "assertive" = CodeRabbit will push back harder on issues
37	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
38	  profile: "assertive"
39	
40	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
41	  # PATH FILTERS — excludes mechanically-generated/derived files from
42	  # review scope entirely (distinct from path_instructions above, which
43	  # only changes review *criteria*, not whether a file is reviewed at
44	  # all). These files are regenerated from other source files already
45	  # covered by path_instructions/code_guidelines below — reviewing the
46	  # derived copy too is redundant, and scripts/hooks/pre-commit already
47	  # blocks hand-editing them directly, so review findings on them can't
48	  # be actioned there anyway. Excluding lock files per CodeRabbit's own
49	  # recommendation (docs.coderabbit.ai/guides/review-instructions).
50	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
51	  path_filters:
52	    - "!package-lock.json"
53	    # Generated by scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs from .claude/rules/*.md + AGENTS.md
54	    - "!.cursor/rules/**"
55	    - "!.vscode/instructions/**"
56	    - "!.github/copilot-instructions.md"
57	    # Generated by scripts/generateRegistry.mjs from overrides/app/
58	    - "!.claude/registry/*.md"
59	
60	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
61	  # PATH-LEVEL INSTRUCTIONS
62	  # This is the most powerful CodeRabbit feature for this project.
63	  # Different review instructions per file path.
64	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
65	  path_instructions:
66	    # ── Repo-wide baseline (was a non-functional top-level `custom_instructions:`
67	    #    key — migrated here since path_instructions is the mechanism that
68	    #    actually exists in the schema; matching entries apply cumulatively
69	    #    alongside the more specific ones below) ─────────────
70	    - path: "overrides/**"
71	      instructions: |
72	        This is a Salesforce Commerce Cloud PWA Kit storefront for Zimmermann luxury fashion.
73	        This is a slim overrides project on `@salesforce/retail-react-app` v10 (not a fork).
74	        The stack is React 18, Chakra UI v2, React Query v4, React Hook Form v7, and Express SSR
75	        on Salesforce Managed Runtime.
76	
77	        For every PR, check:
78	
79	        1. TYPESCRIPT-ONLY INSIDE overrides/ — Every file created or modified under `overrides/`
80	           must use `.ts` or `.tsx`. Flag any `.js`/`.jsx` introduced inside `overrides/`.
81	
82	        2. SSR SAFETY — Any hook or component that accesses window, document, localStorage, or
83	           sessionStorage must have a typeof window !== 'undefined' guard. SSR failures cause
84	           complete page breakdowns.
85	
86	        3. REACT QUERY CACHE — Any mutation that changes basket, customer, or order state must
87	           call queryClient.invalidateQueries() with the correct query key. Missing invalidations
88	           cause stale data that persists until page reload.
89	
90	        4. CHAKRA THEME USAGE — No inline style values for colours, spacing, or typography.
91	           All values must reference theme tokens (e.g. "brand.primary" not "#1A1A1A").
92	           Hard-coded values bypass the design system and break brand consistency.
93	
94	        5. LOCALE AWARENESS — No hardcoded strings in JSX. All user-facing copy must use
95	           react-intl's useIntl() hook and a message ID. Zimmermann serves 18 locales across
96	           6 regions.
97	
98	        6. MULTI-REGION SAFETY — No hardcoded currency symbols, country codes, or locale strings.
99	           Zimmermann serves AU, US, UK, EU, ME, HK (7–8 SFCC sites — US split is TBC).
100	           Use useMultiSite() for site context.
101	
102	        7. EINSTEIN & DATACLOUD EVENTS — Any user interaction that qualifies as a commerce event
103	           (view product, add to cart, begin checkout, click recommendation) must fire the
104	           corresponding Einstein and DataCloud event. Missing events corrupt analytics and
105	           personalisation data.
106	
107	        8. ACCESSIBILITY — Target WCAG 2.2 AA. All interactive elements must have accessible
108	           labels. Images must have alt text. Focus management must be correct in modals and
109	           drawers.
110	
111	        9. PERFORMANCE — Mobile page speed is a top priority. Flag any new synchronous blocking
112	           operations in the SSR render path. Flag any new third-party scripts loaded without
113	           async/defer. Flag images rendered at full resolution where a thumbnail size is used.
114	
115	        10. NO CONSOLE LOGS IN PRODUCTION CODE — Debug logs must be removed before merge.
116	            Sensitive data (tokens, customer PII, basket contents) must never be logged.
117	
118	        11. CLAUDE CODE PROVENANCE — If a PR description or commit message indicates Claude Code CLI
119	            was used to generate the changes, apply heightened scrutiny to shared hooks and
120	            components. Verify the scope of changes matches what was described in the PR.
121	
122	        12. CONVENTIONAL COMMITS — Every commit message in this PR must follow the format:
123	            type(scope): description
124	            Valid types: feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, perf, test, build, ci, chore, upstream-sync
125	            Scope is optional but encouraged (e.g. product-tile, checkout, global-e, contentful).
126	            If any commit does not follow this format (excluding Merge and Revert commits), flag it
127	            and request it be amended before merge. A non-compliant commit message will produce an
128	            incorrect or unclassifiable changelog entry.

CI/CD Pipeline (`.github/workflows/`) **`qa.yml`** — required check on PRs to `develop` and `release/**`. - `detect-changes` job: computes `storybook`/`e2e`/`vitest` booleans via `tj-actions/changed-files` (`files_yaml` allow-lists), diffed against **previous push** (`since_last_remote_commit: true`) not merge-base, so a docs-only follow-up commit doesn't re-trigger heavy suites just because an earlier commit in the PR touched something relevant. Job-level `if:` (not `on.paths`) is used deliberately — a skipped job still reports "success" for required-check purposes, whereas a workflow that never triggers leaves the check stuck "Expected" forever. - **Change-scoped E2E**: `Compute E2E scope` step narrows to `checkout` only if *every* e2e-relevant changed file is inside the `e2e_checkout` allow-list (order-summary/promo-code/pickup-or-delivery/product-tile/product-item/display-price + `e2e/tests/zimm/checkout/**` + `e2e/features/checkout/**`); any file outside all areas falls back to `full`. `release/**`-targeted PRs always get `full`. - **Jira/BrowserStack story scoping**: `Detect Jira story keys` regexes `SFCC-[0-9]+` out of PR title/body/branch (`env:` used to avoid injection from attacker-controlled PR text). `e2e-browserstack` job only runs on develop-targeted PRs when a key was found (grep-scoped to `@SFCC-NNN`); `release/**` PRs always run the full `e2e/tests/zimm` suite unscoped. - **Dependency-change detection**: `Check whether runtime dependencies changed` diffs `package.json`'s `dependencies` block only (not full lockfile) between pushes, forcing `e2e`/`vitest` on if a real runtime dep changed. - Jobs: `unit-tests` (Vitest), `storybook-test` (`@storybook/test-runner` against built Storybook, includes `@storybook/addon-a11y` checks), `e2e-localhost` (Playwright chromium + mobile-chrome against `localhost:3000`/SFCC dev org, 15-min timeout tuned from a measured incident), `e2e-browserstack`. - **No Lighthouse gate in qa.yml** — Lighthouse/perf budget lives only in `digital-sit.yml` (release-branch gate), not on every `develop` PR. **`protected-file-guard.yml`** — triggers on PRs to `develop`/`main`/`release/**`. - `tier1-guard`: **non-blocking** (not a required check) — posts a loud warning + owner-contact-map if any Tier 1 path changed. The doc explains *why* it can't be a required check: GitHub locked down cross-run check-run status updates (Feb 2025), so a "fail until reviewed, flip to pass" pattern is no longer implementable. The real gate is CODEOWNERS + `Require review from Code Owners` branch protection (native GitHub, no Actions involvement). - `branch-target-guard`: **hard block** (`exit 1`) — rejects a PR from a `feature/*` head branch targeting `main` directly. - `tier2-warning`: non-blocking — posts/updates a PR comment listing changed Tier 2 files with a required-second-reviewer checklist. - `cross-squad-guard`: non-blocking — posts a PR comment when a PR touches both Squad A territory (checkout/cart/payments/multiship) and Squad B territory (home/PDP/PLP/search/account/store-locator) in one diff. **`digital-sit.yml`** ("SIT Gate") — on push/PR to `release/**`. Jobs: `playwright-p0` (project `p0`), `lighthouse-ci` (`lhci autorun`, root `lighthouserc.js`; publishes to LHCI server via `LHCI_SERVER_BASE_URL`/`LHCI_TOKEN` secrets if set, else temporary public storage), `contract-tests` (MuleSoft — currently a stub, `npm run test:contracts` echoes a TODO), `bundle-size` (`npm run test:max-file-size` = build + `bundlesize`). `sit-gate` job aggregates all four with `always()` + explicit result checks, `exit 1` if any failed. **`deploy-dev.yml`** (push to `develop`) — `contract-tests` + `bundle-size` gate (`dev-gate`) before `deploy-dev` (`npm run push:dev`, `MRT_USER`/`MRT_API_KEY` secrets) and a `tag-sprint` job that tags `sprint//` when `scripts/sprint.txt` changes. **`deploy-sit.yml`** — `workflow_run` trigger, only deploys if the upstream "SIT Gate" workflow concluded `success`. **`deploy-stg.yml`**/**`deploy-uat.yml`**/**`deploy-prod.yml`** — all `workflow_dispatch` only (manual, ref-input), no automatic trigger; `deploy-prod` has no gate job at all (fully manual promotion). **`upstream-release-watch.yml`** — weekly cron, opens a GitHub issue (`upstream-sync` label) when `SalesforceCommerceCloud/pwa-kit`'s latest release tag differs from the `` marker in `.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md`; dedupes via existing open issue check. **`weekly-agents.yml`** — weekly cron: `quality-sweep` (finds components/hooks under `overrides/app/components`+`hooks` missing both a story and a test, opens/updates a `quality-sweep` issue), `contentful-drift-audit` (finds orphaned `*ContentfulDefinition.ts` files with no paired component), `changelog-reminder` (comments on open release-targeted PRs missing a `/generate-changelog` comment). ### 2. CODEOWNERS Routes every Tier 1 path (theme foundation, Tier-1 hooks, `config/`, `overrides/app/ssr.*`, `worker/main.js`, `mobify.config.js`, root `package.json`, test/tooling configs, `.github/workflows/`, governance files) to `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`. Tier 2 paths route to the specific squad team (`@ZimmermannAU/pwa-squad-a` or `-b`, or both for shared shell) **plus** `@ZimmermannAU/tier-2-approvers` **plus** `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` (project decision: Tier 1 approvers can also clear Tier 2). Tier 3 (squad ownership, e.g. `overrides/app/pages/cart/`→Squad A, `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/`→Squad B) gets *only* the owning squad team, no approver gate. `e2e/` routes to `@ZimmermannAU/pwa-qa-team` (untiered, plain ownership for auto-requested review). ### 3. AI PR review tooling **`coderabbit.yaml`**: `profile: assertive`, `request_changes_workflow: true`. `path_instructions` gives per-path review criteria (repo-wide `overrides/**` baseline covering TS-only, SSR window/document guards, React Query invalidation, Chakra tokens, i18n, multi-region, Einstein/DataCloud events, a11y, perf, no console.log, conventional commits) plus escalated Tier-1/Tier-2-specific instructions for `theme/foundation/**`, `use-current-basket.ts`, `use-current-customer.ts`, `use-navigation.ts`, `use-multi-site.ts`, `config/**`, `mobify.config.js`, `.github/workflows/**`, `ssr.js`, `header/**`, `routes.tsx`, `product-tile/**`, `display-price/**`, checkout/PDP/PLP pages, `e2e/features/**`. `tools:` enables `eslint`, `gitleaks` (secret detection), `ast-grep` (pointed at `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules`), `osvScanner` (OSV.dev dependency vuln scan), `reactDoctor`, and `semgrep` (`config_file: semgrep.yml`). `pre_merge_checks`: `title`/`description` = `error` mode (conventional-commits format enforced), `issue_assessment` = `warning` (Jira Forge app not yet installed), a custom check `Docstring convention compliance` = `error` mode enforcing JSDoc on shared components/exported hooks/non-obvious utils. `path_filters` excludes derived files (`.cursor/rules/**`, `.vscode/instructions/**`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.claude/registry/*.md`, `package-lock.json`) from review entirely. **`.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/`** (3 rules + shared util): - `img-missing-alt.yml` — flags `` without an `alt` attribute (severity warning). - `icon-button-missing-aria-label.yml` — flags `IconButton*` without `aria-label`. - `clickable-non-interactive-element.yml` — flags `div|span|Box|Flex|Stack|VStack|HStack|Grid|Text|PopoverFooter|PopoverHeader` with `onClick` but no `role`. - `utils/jsx-element.yml` — shared `jsxElement` matcher (any `jsx_opening_element`/`jsx_self_closing_element`) reused by the three rules above. **`semgrep.yml`** (2 rules, TypeScript, requires this file to exist at repo root for CodeRabbit to run Semgrep at all): - `payment-credential-logged` (ERROR, taint mode) — sources: any variable/param matching `(?i)(cardNumber|cvv|pin|cardNum|pan)`; sinks: `console.$METHOD(...)`, `Sentry.$METHOD(...)`. - `dangerously-set-inner-html-unsanitized` (ERROR) — flags `dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{__html: $X}}` unless `$X` is `$SANITIZER.sanitize(...)`. ### 4. Git hooks Wired via **Husky v9** (`.husky/pre-commit`, `.husky/commit-msg` — thin wrappers delegating to `scripts/hooks/`), installed automatically by the `"prepare": "husky"` script in `package.json` on `npm install`. Manual fallback documented in `scripts/hooks/README.md` (`cp scripts/hooks/{pre-commit,commit-msg} .git/hooks/`). **`scripts/hooks/pre-commit`** (4 stages, first ensures `node` is on PATH via nvm/fnm/volta fallback): 1. Regenerates `.claude/registry/` when staged files touch `overrides/app/{components,hooks,utils,pages}/` or `routes.tsx`, auto-stages result. 2. Regenerates `.cursor/rules/`/`.vscode/instructions/`/`.github/copilot-instructions.md` via `scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs --fix` when a `.claude/rules/*.md` or `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md` source is staged; warns (non-blocking) to update `.claude/skills/README.md` and the mirrored Confluence page if a skill file changed. 3. Contentful Studio Experiences codegen: regenerates `definitions.ts` from staged `experiences/*.tsx` files (in a temp dir combining staged + working-tree copies) — **blocks commit** (`exit 1`) on codegen failure. 4. **Derived-config guard** — blocks (`exit 1`) any *modified* (not newly-added) `.cursor/rules/*`, `.vscode/instructions/*`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md` file whose `synced-from:` header source isn't also staged in the same commit. 5. **`.env.sample` secret guard** — blocks (`exit 1`) if any key matching `_SECRET|_TOKEN|_PASSWORD|_CREDENTIAL|_PRIVATE_KEY|_API_KEY|_BEARER|_SIGNING_KEY|_ENCRYPTION_KEY|_DSN|_WEBHOOK_SECRET` has a non-empty value, or any value looks like a JWT (`^eyJ...`), 32+ char hex, 40+ char base64, or a known provider prefix (`AKIA...`, `ghp_...`, `ghs_...`, `sk-...`, `xox[bpars]-...`). **`scripts/hooks/commit-msg`** — enforces conventional-commits regex `^(feat|fix|docs|style|refactor|perf|test|build|ci|chore|upstream-sync)(\([a-z0-9/._-]+\))?: .{1,100}$`, exempting `Merge`/`Revert`/`fixup!`/`squash!`/`WIP` prefixes; `exit 1` + a full usage help message on mismatch. ### 5. TypeScript / lint / build enforcement **`tsconfig.json`**: `noEmit: true` (Babel transpiles), `strict: true`, `isolatedModules: true`, `skipLibCheck: true`, path aliases `~/*`→`./*`, `app/*`→`./overrides/app/*`, `include: ["overrides/**/*", "vitest.config.ts", "vitest.setup.ts"]`. **`.eslintrc.js`**: extends `@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/configs/eslint` (base); `overrides` block scopes `@typescript-eslint` rules to `.ts`/`.tsx` (via `parserOptions.project`) and sets `no-floating-promises`, `no-inferrable-types`, `restrict-template-expressions`, `no-misused-promises`, `require-await` all to `warn` (not `error`). **Confirms AGENTS.md's claim**: no `max-lines-per-function` or `complexity` rule is configured anywhere in this file — the ~150-line/complexity guidance in `.claude/rules/components.md` is genuinely unenforced by ESLint. **`babel.config.js`**: extends `@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/configs/babel/babel-config`, adds `babel-plugin-module-resolver` for the same `~`/`app` aliases (kept in sync with tsconfig/vitest/storybook per comments in each file). **`package.json`** key scripts: `lint` (`pwa-kit-dev lint "overrides/**/*.{ts,tsx}"`), `test` (`vitest run`), `build` (`build-translations && pwa-kit-dev build`), `push`/`push:` (build + `pwa-kit-dev push -t `), `test:lighthouse` (`lhci autorun --config=tests/lighthouserc.js` — note: this references `tests/lighthouserc.js`, a path that does **not currently exist** on disk; only root `lighthouserc.js` exists and is what `digital-sit.yml` actually runs against via default resolution), `test:max-file-size` (build + `bundlesize`), `test:contracts` (stub, always exits 0), `env` (`scripts/switchEnv.mjs`). `bundlesize` config: `build/main.js` ≤180kB, `build/vendor.js` ≤550kB. `browserslist`: iOS≥17, Android≥14, last 4 ChromeAndroid. ### 6. Test harness config **`vitest.config.ts`**: `environment: 'jsdom'`, `setupFiles: ['./vitest.setup.ts']`, `include: ['overrides/**/*.test.ts', 'overrides/**/*.test.tsx']`, `passWithNoTests: true`, same `~`/`app` aliases. No coverage-threshold config present. **`vitest.setup.ts`** — just imports `@testing-library/jest-dom`. **`playwright.config.js`**: `testDir: './e2e'`, `testMatch: '**/*.spec.js'`, `forbidOnly: !!process.env.CI`, `retries: 2` (CI only), `workers: 1`. Projects: `p0` (SIT gate, 0 retries), `chromium`/`mobile-chrome` (exclude a11y/mobile-or-desktop/`extra-features.spec.js`), `a11y-mobile`/`a11y-desktop` (dedicated `testDir`), `extra-features-desktop`/`-mobile`. **`.storybook/main.js`**: stories glob `../overrides/**/*.stories.@(js|jsx|ts|tsx|mdx)`, addons include `@storybook/addon-a11y`; `webpackFinal` aliases `@salesforce/retail-react-app`/`pwa-kit-react-sdk`/`pwa-kit-runtime`/`commerce-sdk-react` to `node_modules`, plus the project `~`/`app` aliases. **`.storybook/preview.tsx`**: `a11y.test: 'error'` — a11y violations **fail** `test-storybook --ci` runs; excludes Chakra's toast-manager regions from a11y checks (known upstream limitation). **`.browserstack.yml`**: `testSuite: e2e/tests/zimm` only (scope enforcement per frozenFiles.md's "scope change = CI cost explosion" note); browsers: Chrome (macOS Sonoma), Safari (macOS Sonoma), Firefox (Windows 11), Edge (Windows 11); `testObservability: true` linking to Zephyr via `buildName: Sprint-${SPRINT_NUMBER}`; `parallelsPerPlatform: 2`. **`lighthouserc.js`**: `numberOfRuns: 3`; assertions — `categories:performance` ≥0.80 (error), `categories:accessibility` ≥0.90 (error), `categories:best-practices` ≥0.90 (error), preset `lighthouse:recommended`; upload target is `lhci` server if `LHCI_SERVER_BASE_URL` set, else `temporary-public-storage`. ### 7. Environment & secrets tooling **`scripts/switchEnv.mjs`** subcommands: (none) → report current tier; `init` → scaffolds `.env.shared` + all six `.env.` files, pulls values from GitHub Environments (`gh variable list --env `), auto-fetches Contentful tokens; `validate [--live]` → cross-checks key placement (shared vs tier vs personal vs auto), flags typos/misplaced keys, and with `--live` makes a real read-only Contentful Delivery API call + a real SLAS guest-token request per tier; `push ` → **gated to tier-1-approvers only** via `isTier1Approver()` (`gh api user --jq .login` + `gh api orgs/ZimmermannAU/teams/tier-1-approvers/members`), excludes `scope:personal` keys from ever being pushed/pulled centrally; `` → merges `.env.shared` + `.env.` into `.env` (tier wins), stamps `ENVIRONMENT_NAME`/`DEPLOY_TARGET`. **`.env.sample`** header documents the full command reference (matches above) plus the `scope:shared|tier|personal|auto` tagging convention — scope tag must be its own comment line above `KEY=value` (not trailing), specifically so a blank placeholder doesn't read as non-empty to the pre-commit secret guard. Documents a deliberate, confirmed override: GitHub Environment Variables are plaintext/readable by any repo collaborator, a conscious tradeoff accepted for centralization (write gated to repo Admin = tier-1-approvers). **Secret-leak prevention**: the pre-commit hook's `.env.sample` guard (section 4 above) is the main mechanical control; `gitleaks` (via `coderabbit.yaml` tools) is a second, PR-time layer. ### 8. Contentful sync safety **`scripts/contentful/sync.js`**: reads `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN`/`CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID`/`CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID`, iterates `.js` files in `scripts/contentful/content-types/` (currently just `shoppableImage.js`), calls `upsertContentType()` per file. **Additive-only confirmed in code**: on update, `ct.fields = [...(ct.fields ?? []).filter(f => !defIds.has(f.id)), ...fields]` — explicitly preserves existing fields not present in the local definition, never deletes a field from a live content type; each type is published after upsert. `.docs/architecture.md` and `AGENTS.md` both state this idempotent/additive behavior, and the code matches. ### 9. Dependency/package protections **No Renovate or Dependabot config found anywhere in the repo** (`find` for `renovate*`/`dependabot*` returned nothing outside `node_modules`) — dependency updates are entirely manual/PR-based, with `coderabbit.yaml`'s `auto_review.ignore_title_keywords: ["chore(deps)", "dependabot"]` implying dependency-bump PRs were anticipated but no bot is actually configured to open them. Root `package.json` is confirmed Tier 1 in `frozenFiles.md`, `CODEOWNERS` (`package.json → @ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`), and `protected-file-guard.yml`'s tier1 file list — consistent across all three enforcement surfaces. `osvScanner` (CodeRabbit tool) provides dependency-vulnerability scanning as a partial substitute for a dependency-bump bot. ### 10. Docs encoding process guardrails - **`.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md`**: back-merge rules (release→main triggers back-merge to develop; hotfix→main same), and the release-branch supervised-edit protocol (state plan → assess blast radius/consumer count → wait for explicit confirmation before any edit) plus the `fix/release-{version}-*` sub-branch requirement for code logic fixes. - **`.docs/architecture.md`** (guardrail-relevant parts): confirms path-alias sync group is actually **5** files, not 4 (`babel.config.js`, `tsconfig.json`, `.storybook/main.js`, `jest.config.js` moduleNameMapper, `vitest.config.ts`) — `jest.config.js` is called out as a separate group for `pwa-kit-dev` internals only, not part of the 4-way sync AGENTS.md describes. Documents the overrides-pattern copy-first flow (copy → convert → `tsc --noEmit` → stop for approval) and SSR mandate (DMU-030 — SSR must be preserved for product/category/content pages, no client-only shortcuts). Also documents `undici` per-origin connection-pool isolation in `overrides/app/ssr.js`/`overrides/app/ssr/connectionPools.ts` as blast-radius mitigation. - **`.docs/upstreamPolicy.md`**: "bump opportunistically, not on a schedule" policy tied to `upstream-release-watch.yml`; explicitly states there is **no drift-detection script** (drift is the point of the overrides pattern) and **no two-track review**. - **`.docs/memory/`** contents: `projectState.md` (current status of all services/integrations/deploy state, updated each session), `feedback.md` (what worked/failed/gotchas learned), `references.md` (service URLs/credentials/dashboard locations), `sprintScope.md` (draft dependency order of the build — gates what Claude may assume exists), `upstreamBaseline.md` (pinned `@salesforce/retail-react-app` version + `` marker consumed by the watch workflow). ### 11. `.claude/settings.json` - **`PreToolUse`** hook on `Write|Edit|NotebookEdit`: (a) blocks any file write if `git branch --show-current` is `develop` or `main` (`exit 1` with a BLOCKED message) — this is the actual mechanical enforcement of Hard Rule #1/#3 in the branch table, not just documentation; (b) runs `.claude/hooks/tier2Warn.sh` if present. - **`PostToolUse`** hooks: on `Write` — auto-runs Prettier on the new file; on `Edit|Write` — runs `.claude/hooks/contentfulDriftWarn.sh` (referenced but not found on disk — dangling reference) and `.claude/hooks/registryUpdate.sh`; on `Write` — runs `.claude/hooks/testFileRemind.sh`. - **`Stop`** hook: runs `.claude/hooks/session-reflect.sh`. - **`permissions.allow`**: pre-approves read-only/low-risk Bash patterns (`git branch/status/diff/log/show`, `find`, `grep`, `ls`, `npm run lint/test/build`, `gh pr/api/issue`) so Claude isn't prompted for these every time. - **`.claude/settings.local.json`** (session-specific, not checked in for team-wide enforcement): allows specific MCP/Bash patterns (`gh api user`, `mcp-atlassian`, `git checkout/fetch`, a specific `WebFetch` domain), `enableAllProjectMcpServers: true`, enables `mcp-atlassian`. Client-side hook scripts (all in `.claude/hooks/`, all **non-blocking**, `exit 0` always): - `tier2Warn.sh` — regex-matches the edited file path against Tier 2 groups (global shell, shared product/commerce components, theme component styles, shared hooks, translations) and prints an owner/notify warning. - `registryUpdate.sh` — incrementally regenerates `.claude/registry/` entries for the specific edited file (components/hooks/utils/pages/routes), skipping test/story/ContentfulDefinition files. - `testFileRemind.sh` — after writing a new component/hook source file, checks for a co-located `.test.*` file and prints a reminder (not a block) if missing. - `session-reflect.sh` — Stop hook that, if anything changed this session, returns `{decision: "block", reason: ...}` forcing Claude to write a proposal file to `.docs/agents-proposals/-.md` suggesting doc updates (AGENTS.md, architecture.md, memory files, rule tiers) — explicitly forbidden from editing those docs directly itself. Has a re-entry guard (`stop_hook_active`) to avoid infinite loop. ### 12. Other guardrails found - **`.claude/rules/squadA.md` / `squadB.md`** — squad territory maps with YAML frontmatter `paths:` lists, consumed by the `scope-check` skill and referenced by `.claude/skills/audit-tier` for Tier 3 classification; not enforced mechanically (draft status noted — "squad split can still change"). - **`.claude/skills/scope-check/SKILL.md`** — a pre-flight tool: classifies every file a proposed prompt would likely touch by tier (1–4), verdicts SAFE/RISKY/BLOCKED, and rewrites unsafe prompts — a guardrail applied *before* Claude acts, not after. - **`scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs`** — the generator behind the pre-commit hook's derived-file sync; supports `--check` (CI-style drift detection, exit 1 on drift) and `--fix` modes; keeps `.cursor/rules/*.mdc`, `.vscode/instructions/*.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md` in sync with `.claude/rules/*.md` + `AGENTS.md` so multiple AI tools see consistent rules. - **`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`** — structured checklist enforcing (via human/reviewer discipline, not CI): squad ownership ticking, breaking-change definition, protection-tier self-check (referencing `/audit-tier`), `npx tsc --noEmit`/lint/test/storybook checklist, WCAG 2.1 AA minimum bar, localisation (18 locale files), third-party-integration degradation notes. - **`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`** — `bug_report.md`, `feature_request.md` (not deeply inspected, standard issue templates). - **No dedicated ast-grep or semgrep config exists outside `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/` and root `semgrep.yml`** — both are Tier 1 per `frozenFiles.md`/CODEOWNERS/`protected-file-guard.yml` consistently. - **Discrepancy worth flagging**: `package.json`'s `test:lighthouse` script points at `tests/lighthouserc.js`, and `frozenFiles.md`/CODEOWNERS both list `tests/lighthouserc.js` as a Tier 1 path — but no `tests/` directory exists in the repo; only the root `lighthouserc.js` is real and is what `digital-sit.yml` actually executes via `lhci autorun` (implicit default config resolution, no `--config` flag passed in the workflow). This is a latent doc/script drift, not a currently-broken gate, since the workflow doesn't reference the missing path directly.
